reading.body:
Troy Carter's AI record is four sponsored or cosponsored AI bills, four recorded votes in favor of AI bills, and thirteen contributions from AI company political committees, all dated between March 2025 and October 2026.

The pattern is legislative activity and committee money running on the same calendar. The contributions come from the PACs of Meta, Google, Microsoft, and Amazon, in amounts of $1,000 to $3,000, and two of them are negative entries, a $3,000 Meta adjustment in February 2026 and a $1,000 Google adjustment in August 2025, which are corrections to earlier filings rather than new money. The bills cover a CISA AI task force, AI for secure networks, a national AI research resource, and deepfake regulation. The votes are all procedural motions to suspend the rules and pass, which is the route used for bills with broad support.

For AI specifically, this is the money-and-legislation layer that sits above compute. The companies funding these committees are the same ones buying power and building data centers, and the bills here touch security and research infrastructure rather than the grid itself. Nothing in this data connects a contribution to a vote or a bill, and the page states that placement in date order is not a claim of causation. The record also does not show committee assignments, floor speeches, or any position on data center siting, utility rates, or interconnection, which is where the binding constraint on AI scaling actually sits.
